mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face production challenges and reduced output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The ratio of RSAFS to GDPC1 shows no significant correlation with 20-day forward returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month signals a robust labor market, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a low inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) below 2% signals a stable economic environment, which encourages the Federal Reserve to maintain accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last six months signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
